title: Service-boundary span anchoring & OTLP proxy ack bridging for durable Tempo ingest
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Enable a lightweight OTLP proxy that anchors service-boundary spans with a durable acknowledgement (ACK) handshake to Tempo-compatible backends. The feature improves delivery guarantees for high-cardinality services by acknowledging receipt at the proxy layer while performing best-effort replay and schema normalization to accommodate Tempo/Jaeger ingest differences. This ticket implements the proxy-side span anchoring, idempotent envelope IDs, tenant-metadata preservation, and a compact retry/TTL policy so downstream storage does not receive duplicates or divergent trace fragments.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy emits per-batch ACK that the ingest controller can return to the service caller within configured latency SLO (<= 15ms median extra per request)
Spans preserved service boundary tags and tenant annotations in the Tempo envelope fields; verified via synthetic trace tests
No duplicated top-level trace segments in Tempo after a replay (idempotency ensured by envelope ID check)
Adaptive backpressure triggers shed low-priority traces without blocking high-priority SLO traffic
Automated e2e test harness demonstrates failover: proxy accepts traces while Tempo is down and replays to Tempo when healthy, with <=0.5% trace loss in 100k-trace run
implementation_notes: Add envelope_id (uuid4) at proxy ingress and persist a 24-hour LRU idempotency cache keyed by (tenant, envelope_id)
Translate legacy jaeger tags into Tempo labels in the proxy normalizer; rely on a small transform pipeline to avoid heavy CPU work
Introduce an ACK response model: proxy responds to upstream with ack_status and short-lived ack_token. Downstream write is async with replay queue persisted to local SSD-backed write-ahead log
Expose metrics: ack_latency_ms, replay_queue_depth, idempotent_drops, tenant_replay_rate
Config flags: probe_mode (dry-run), ack_latency_slo_ms, replay_ttl_hours, retention_of_ack_tokens
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope id generation and idempotency cache eviction
Integration test: synthetic workload (50k traces) with intermittent Tempo downtime to validate replay correctness
Chaos test: network partition between proxy and Tempo to validate ack behavior and queue growth handling
Performance test: measure added p99 latency per request with proxy enabled on representative service images
Golden trace comparison script that checks for duplicates and ordering violations after replay
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - feature gate off: deploy proxy binary in canary namespace with probe_mode=true (no acks) for 48 hours
Stage 2 - limited tenants: enable ack model for 5 low-risk tenants and monitor idempotent_drops and replay_queue_depth for 72 hours
Stage 3 - ramp: increase tenant percentage by 25% increments while maintaining sat checks; enable alerting thresholds
Stage 4 - global enable: flip feature gate for all tenants and decommission temporary debug hooks after 1 week of stable telemetry
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: ACK path adds latency to hot request flows. Mitigation: async ack_token issuance and config knob to prefer best-effort ack with <15ms median overhead
Risk: Idempotency cache can grow for high-cardinality tenants. Mitigation: LRU with tenant-scoped quotas and metrics to trigger eviction alerts
Risk: Replay floods Tempo on recovery. Mitigation: token-bucket rate limiter and progressive backoff with per-tenant caps
Risk: Schema mismatch between Jaeger envelopes and Tempo. Mitigation: lightweight normalizer rules with fallbacks to raw attribute mapping and a compatibility test suite
